items.title: The 15-Minute Pre-Submit Resume QA Pipeline
items.pt:
You can spend a weekend rewriting bullets and still lose the interview to a parsing break, a phone number ATS cannot tokenize, or three fluff lines that make a semantic screener score you as generic. The fix is not another rewrite. It is a short, boring, repeatable QA pipeline you run every time before you hit Apply, the same way you run tests before you ship.

I wrote this with help from AI tools and checked every checklist item, lint snippet and before/after example myself. I build Smart Resu

items.title: How to get a Slack alert when a company posts a new job (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) with n8n or Python
items.pt:
Whether you're job hunting, selling to companies that are hiring, or keeping an eye on competitors, "tell me when Stripe posts a new role" is a surprisingly annoying problem. Career pages don't have RSS. Job board alerts miss postings, duplicate them, and arrive days late.

Most companies host their career page on an applicant tracking system (ATS) like Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby, and those have public job feeds. The tricky part isn't fetching jobs. It's remembering which ones you've already see

items.title: Give yourself a payday: the one habit that steadies freelance income
items.pt:
A salary arrives on a fixed date. Freelance money does not. It lands on a Tuesday, then nothing for three weeks, then two payments in one day. A budget that tries to follow that rhythm will always feel behind.

The fix is simple, and it sounds almost too simple: give yourself a payday. Pick one date a month, and pay yourself a fixed amount on that date, from money that has already cleared.

For the rest of the month, client payments go into a holding pot, not into your spending. You do not spend

items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
items.pt: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.pt: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. items.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
items.pt: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample
